
`lode doc note <doc>#sec-N --body "..."` attaches a note to the section at that anchor, linked to the task and session that raised it. It never blocks execution. Two callers: an executor recording a defect it is not fixing, and a fixer recording what it changed and why. A note is stored as a bare thread in `review_threads` (WL-REQ-1319) anchored to the section alone (`doc_anchor`, no byte range or quote), so editing the section's text never makes it `obsolete`. Notes surface in `lode doc list --has-notes` and on the review view. Note volume is the design-quality signal. Agents never autonomously write an `amends` edge between rules, because it changes how the corpus reads the amended rule.
